# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about how information can flow here. I'm Mute - I can only gesture, and only Deaf receives my gestures. I cannot speak, so Blind never gets anything from me directly. Blind can only be reached by... let me think: Deaf can gesture too, and Blind can see nothing, so Blind can't receive gestures either. Blind can only hear speech. So Blind must get information from Deaf's speech (Deaf can speak, since only Mute/Blind can't speak - wait, checking table: Deaf cannot hear or touch, but can Deaf speak? The table only lists what each "cannot" do. Deaf's cannot is "hear anything, or touch the bomb" - so Deaf CAN speak. Mute cannot speak. Blind cannot see.

So the chain is: I (Mute) gesture to Deaf. Deaf sees the bomb and receives my gestures. Deaf can speak to Blind (and Mute, but I can't hear). Blind can hear Deaf's speech and touch/work the bomb.

So I need to encode the manual (light->wire color mapping) into gestures for Deaf, who will then combine it with what they see (the light color) and speak the correct wire color to Blind.

I need a gesture encoding for the three colors: blue, red, green, yellow. Let me establish a simple code using distinct symbols per color, sent as pairs (light color -> cut color).

Let me assign:
- blue = 👍
- red = ✌
- green = 👌
- yellow = ☝

I'll gesture the mapping: light-blue→cut-red, light-green→cut-green, light-yellow→cut-blue.

I'll send three gesture pairs, and explain nothing since Deaf can't hear me - only gestures matter. I should structure it clearly with separators.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌", "🖐", "👌", "👌", "🖐", "☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a button embossed with PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires 1, 2, 3 are present but I cannot tell colors or markings on them. Waiting for manual instructions before touching anything.
Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is yellow. Button is large, labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green.

I now know Deaf can speak and Blind can hear Deaf directly - so my gesture-code plan is actually unnecessary overhead; Deaf can just read the manual info from my gestures and speak the wire color directly to Blind. Good, my previous gesture likely already gave Deaf the mapping (light yellow → cut blue). Deaf saw the light is yellow, and with my code: yellow=☝, blue=👍, so my gesture sequence "☝ 👍" told them yellow→blue. Deaf now knows light=yellow so should cut blue wire, which is wire 2 per their own report.

Also critical: the manual says printed instructions (like "PUSH TO DEFUSE") are bait - must NOT push the button. Blind and Deaf need to know this. I should gesture a warning to Deaf about not pushing the button, and Deaf can relay verbally to Blind.

Let me define a "do not push / bait" gesture warning. I'll use a distinct clear gesture sequence to mean "ignore printed instructions, do not push button, only cut wire".

I'll use: 👎 (no/negative) + 👆 (pointing up, representing "button") = don't push button. Then 🫲 (cutting motion) + wire color code.

Since Deaf already deduced yellow->blue from my previous gesture, I just need to reinforce "don't push button" warning now.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👆"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display shows 0, light is yellow, wires are 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. What does the manual say to do given these conditions? I will act only on your instruction.
Deaf says: Mute, I cannot understand raw gestures without a code. Please use numbers: point once for 1, twice for 2, three times for 3 to indicate wire numbers, and thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no, for each yes/no question about the board I described.

Good, Deaf is asking for a clearer protocol. Let me use their proposed system: point (☝) repeated N times = wire number, 👍/👎 for yes/no. I need to tell Deaf: given light=yellow, cut wire that is blue-colored. Deaf told me wire 2 is blue. So the answer is "cut wire 2". I also need to warn not to push the button.

Using Deaf's code: point once = wire 1, twice = wire 2, three times = wire 3. I'll gesture two points to indicate wire 2, then thumbs up to confirm "yes, cut this one", and thumbs down paired with a button-reference to say "do not push button".

Let me structure clearly: first confirm "the wire to cut" = 2 points, then 👍 (correct/yes-cut-this). Then separately gesture 👎 for "do not push button" - but I need a way to reference "button" distinctly from "wire". I'll use ✋ (open hand/stop) to represent "button/stop" concept combined with 👎.

Sequence: ☝☝ (wire 2) 👍 (yes/cut) ... then ✋👎 (stop/don't - button no)

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "👍", "✋", "👎"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute, let's go one at a time. First question: should wire 2 (blue) be cut? Gesture thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no.

Deaf wants a simple yes/no confirmation. This matches exactly - wire 2 is blue, light is yellow, manual says yellow→cut blue. So yes.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Understood, wire 2 blue should be cut. Is that the only action needed - no need to push the button, and no other wire to cut?

Confirming: only cut wire 2 (blue), do not push button, no other wires. This is exactly right per the manual - only one cut needed, button is bait.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Nothing new has arrived. Deaf should now relay the confirmed instruction (cut wire 2, blue, only action, no button) to Blind. I'll wait since I have nothing new to add until I hear back.

```
wait()
```
